messages:
june-k: Quick ping after today's security review with ACME. They want a deliverable they can hand to auditors: a signed "proof-pack" for a 7-day window (logs, RBAC changes, egress summaries), with key custody attestation and the ability to re-identify pseudonymized PII under auditor control. Is that doable without a major project?

sarah-lee: short answer: yes for a Hosted PoC using our signing key + strong manifests. CMK per-tenant for hosted requires extra KMS grant flows. For Private we can support HSM-backed signing immediately. I'll outline 3 delivery options.

matt-b: option 1 (hosted PoC, fastest): produce ndjson logs gzipped, manifest.json with entry hashes (we'll use sha512), and a detached signature (sig.der) computed by our signing service. Include KMS access audit (who called Sign) and the x509 attestation bundle mapping key id -> cert.

option 2 (hosted w/ CMK): support customer-supplied KMS key (ARN) to sign manifest. Need automated grant provisioning + expiry, plus operator approval flow. Estimate: ~2 sprints infra + 1 sprint security attestation work.

option 3 (private/on-prem): customer HSM hosts signing keys; we produce manifest and hand signature process over. Minimal infra work on our side.

owen-secbot: Incident-bot: flagged dependent CVE-2026-9876 in log-processor. Recommend freeze on signing exports until patch is verified.

matt-b: patch progress: log-processor -> 2.4.2 deployed to prod-1; canary green. we'll include a "software_inventory" header in the manifest with versions and CVE scan timestamp.

sarah-lee: on pseudonymization: we can replace emails with tenant-scoped pseudonyms. Two modes:
- irreversible hash: HMAC-SHA256(email, tenant_salt) -> good for privacy but cannot re-id.
- reversible mapping: store mapping encrypted with a wrapping key; decrypt only with auditor-approved KMS decrypt call; every decrypt is logged in KMS audit.

june-k: ACME prefers reversible re-id (auditor may need to map). They also want proof no exfil occurred in window.

matt-b: for egress proof we can bundle network_flow summaries, object-store access logs, and signed manifests of objects produced in window. Full S3 logs can be large; propose targeted buckets + manifest hashes. We'll add a tombstone list for deleted/expired objects.

sarah-lee: sample manifest structure:
```
{
  "exported_at": "2026-03-18T16:12:00Z",
  "window": { "from": "2026-03-11T00:00:00Z", "to": "2026-03-18T00:00:00Z" },
  "service_versions": { "log-processor": "2.4.2", "auth": "1.9.0" },
  "entries": [
    { "path": "audit/tenant-ACME/2026-03-12/events.ndjson.gz", "sha512": "a7b..." },
    { "path": "rbac/tenant-ACME/role-changes.csv.gz", "sha512": "c5d..." }
  ]
}
```
Signature computed over the canonicalized manifest bytes (no whitespace) using KMS Sign or HSM.

unece: action: what about RBAC audit exports? ACME needs an ordered change log for service accounts (who, when, previous/new role).

matt-b: we already index IAM events. We'll export CSV: timestamp, actor, target_principal, change_type, role_before, role_after, runbook_ref. Automation rotations will show actor=rotation-service; we'll include runbook_ref to map to human owner.

sarah-lee: legal check: if reversible mapping uses customer CMK, auditors can re-id only if we've configured decrypt grants. If we wrap with our key, we need strong attestation we won't re-id without their approval. legal, can you confirm acceptable pattern?

legal: We prefer customer-controlled keys for re-id. If not possible, require written auditor oversight + signed approval recorded in our logs. Also confirm retention windows for mapping files.

matt-b: verification example for auditors (openssl):
```
# verify manifest signature (DER)
openssl dgst -sha512 -verify pubkey.pem -signature sig.der manifest.json
```
If KMS sign used, we'll supply attestation cert chain and the key id.

sarah-lee: we'll also include a "retention_proof" file: purge-run logs with tombstone entries and timestamps; and a retention_policy.json describing rule ids and last-run timestamps.

owen-secbot: action list generated: ["POC_signed_export_hosted" -> @sarah-lee,@matt-b due 2026-03-25, "CMK_signing_feasibility_doc" -> @sarah-lee due 2026-04-08, "RBAC_csv_proto" -> @matt-b,@tara-r due 2026-03-23, "Legal_pseudonym_policy_check" -> @june-k,@legal due 2026-03-20].

june-k: perfect. scheduling follow-up demo with ACME 2026-03-26. thanks team. :raised_hands:

matt-b: will post PoC artifacts to internal bucket and drop link here once ready.

sarah-lee: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/proof-pack-export

june-k: closing loop with ACME after we have PoC.
